dedupe_keys.name: industrial demand side flexibility benchmark data set kit

description: This dataset gives benchmark instances for scheduling time-flexible industrial processes by power demand, published with the 2019 ACM e-Energy paper "Industrial Demand-Side Flexibility: A Benchmark Data Set". The KITopen page says each JSON file in the instances folder is one scheduling instance, in a format usable with the TCPSPSuite optimisation software, with the generator parameters stored per instance; the results folder has baseline solutions, best lower bounds and MIP gaps, and a decompositions file lists energy and duration blocks of motif occurrences found in measured production data. It was created on 30 April 2019 by Nicole Ludwig, Lukas Barth, Dorothea Wagner and Veit Hagenmeyer of KIT's Institute for Automation and Applied Informatics and Institute of Theoretical Computer Science, free to download under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is generated instances derived from one German production site. Caveats: the raw time series could not be published (a subset is in the separate HIPE data set), and the archive size is not stated on the page read. For simulation it gives realistic test cases for optimising when factories shift load to support the grid. Related catalogue records include the VEA industrial load profiles and the IMDELD industrial machines dataset.
